props.name: above 100 atm and 200 °C, catalyst below 600 °C; preferred 100-200 atm, 250-300 °C

evidence.quote: Pressures in excess of 100 atmospheres and temperatures in excess of 200° C. should be is employed.
The reaction temperature—i. e., of the catalyst mass—should not exceed 600° - C.
In general, we prefer to use pressures between 100-200 atmosphere and a temperature of 250-300° C.
At pressures and temperatures within the range described, methanol will be produced in every case by the use of our copper alloy catalysts.

props.scope: methanol synthesis over the copper-alloy catalysts
props.statement: Pressures above 100 atmospheres and temperatures above 200° C. should be employed, the catalyst temperature not exceeding 600° C.; no definite upper pressure limit; preferred 100-200 atmospheres and 250-300° C. Within this range methanol is produced in every case with the copper alloy catalysts.

props.name: oxidation makes the surface irregular and porous

evidence.quote: the surface of the catalyst is rendered irregular and porous.

On ex- @g posure to a reducing atmosphere, such as hy- drogen gas, the oxidized surface is partially reduced to metal and the complex mixture of copper alloy and derived oxides constitutes . an active. methanol catalyst.

props.statement: During the oxidation the surface of the catalyst is rendered irregular and porous; on reduction the oxidized surface is partially reduced to metal and the mixture of copper alloy and derived oxides is the active catalyst.
